_readme: Our own English translation of the Testament of Job, made for this app directly from
the Greek of manuscript P as transcribed by the Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, which
is public domain. Their eclectic texts of Brock and Kraft are licensed from Brill and
were NOT used; nor was Spittler's translation in Charlesworth, which is in copyright.
Keys are 'chapter.verse', matching the transcription's own numbering — the division
M. R. James established, which Brock and Charlesworth follow, so scholarly citations
P is an 11th-century witness with real irregularities: it spells Job's wife's name
variously across chapters and has occasional itacistic slips. The translation renders
the sense, normalising obvious slips; square brackets mark words supplied for sense.
build-tjob-greek.py hides English entirely until every verse is translated, so students
1.1: The book of the words of Job, who is called Jobab.
1.2: For on the day when he fell ill and was settling his affairs, he called his seven sons and his three daughters,
1.3: whose names are these: Tersi, Choros, Hyon, Nike, Phoros, Phiphe, Phrouon, Hemera, Kasia, and Amaltheia's Horn.
1.4: And when he had called his children he said: Gather round me, my children, gather round, so that I may show you what the Lord did with me, and everything that has happened to me.
1.5: For I am Job your father, who lived in all endurance; and you are a chosen and honoured race, from the seed of Jacob, the father of your mother.
1.6: For I am of the sons of Esau, the brother of Jacob, whose daughter Dinah is your mother, by whom I fathered you — for my former wife died a bitter death, together with ten other children. Listen to me then, my children, and I will make plain to you what has befallen me.
